mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in the federal funds rate below 0.1% signals an aggressive monetary easing stance by the Fed, which typically boosts investor confidence and increases liquidity in the market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS drops below 0.1% within a 20-day horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 1% within a month signals economic distress, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors react to the deteriorating economic conditions.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in > 50% of instances when UNRATE increases by more than 1% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which is a positive indicator for corporate earnings and thus leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in > 40% of instances when RSAFS increases for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in a month signals a supply shock, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as companies face production challenges and reduced output.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in > 60% of instances when INDPRO drops by more than 2% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 10% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) decrease by more than 500,000 in a month, it signals severe labor market distress, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investor sentiment worsens.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in > 50% of instances when UNRATE > 10% and PAYEMS decrease > 500,000.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) increase by more than 10% in a month and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) remains stable (less than 0.5% change), it signals strong demand without inflationary pressure, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in > 40% of instances when HOUST increases > 10% and CPIAUCSL change < 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 3% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 2% in a quarter, it signals tightening monetary conditions with inflationary pressure, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 3% and CPIAUCSL increases > 2% in a quarter
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 3% and CPIAUCSL increases > 2% in a quarter.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) increases by more than 5% in a quarter and GDP (GDPC1) grows by more than 2%, it signals robust economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to rise.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in > 40% of instances when INDPRO increases > 5% and GDPC1 > 2%.
